claim.pdf_says: In 14.9.48.2 the following words are printed with underlines (required words): UNSTRING, DELIMITED, ALL (both occurrences), OR, INTO, DELIMITER, COUNT, POINTER, TALLYING, OVERFLOW (both occurrences), NOT, END-UNSTRING. BY, WITH, IN and ON are printed WITHOUT underlines (optional words).
claim.markdown_says: "UNSTRING identifier-1" ... "| DELIMITED BY [ ALL ] { identifier-2 } [ OR [ ALL ] { identifier-3 } ] … |" ... "INTO { identifier-4 [ DELIMITER IN identifier-5 ] [ COUNT IN identifier-6 ] } …" ... "[ WITH POINTER identifier-7 ]" ... "[ TALLYING IN identifier-8 ]" ... "[ END-UNSTRING ]" - no underline markup anywhere and no '> **Figure notes ...**' paragraph after the figure (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32372-32392).
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining is the standard's only marker separating required words from optional words (5.2.6.2). With it gone and no figure-notes paragraph to carry the information, the transcription cannot tell an implementer that BY, WITH and IN are omissible while DELIMITED, POINTER and TALLYING are not. Every other code-fenced statement figure in this file records the underlines in a figure note (START 31759, STRING 31970, CALL 25700, SEND 30641, SET 30770-30838), so UNSTRING is an unswept gap rather than a different convention.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by independent inspection of the 300 dpi render of spec_p799.png (printed page 769, section 14.9.48 UNSTRING), plus a 2x crop of the general-format figure and a 3x crop of the ON OVERFLOW group. Every particular of the claim's PDF description holds when the glyphs are read directly. Underlined (required): UNSTRING; DELIMITED; ALL in 'DELIMITED BY [ ALL ]'; OR; ALL in 'OR [ ALL ]'; INTO; DELIMITER; COUNT; POINTER; TALLYING; OVERFLOW in 'ON OVERFLOW'; NOT; OVERFLOW in 'NOT ON OVERFLOW'; END-UNSTRING. Not underlined (optional): BY; IN at all three occurrences (DELIMITER IN, COUNT IN, TALLYING IN); WITH; ON at both occurrences. The underlines are unambiguous rules drawn beneath the words, not artifacts - e.g. in 'NOT ON OVERFLOW' the rule sits under NOT and under OVERFLOW with a clean unruled gap under ON, and in '[ WITH POINTER identifier-7 ]' the rule starts at POINTER and stops before identifier-7. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32372-32395 carries none of it: plain text with no underscores, no <u>, no bold, no other required-word marker, and `grep -n 'Figure notes (UNSTRING'` over the whole file returns nothing (exit 1), so no figure note anywhere recovers the distinction. The convention the claim appeals to is real and is the file's established practice - 225 '> **Figure notes ...**' paragraphs exist, and the two nearest sibling statements both have one: START at line 31762 and STRING at line 31973, each naming exactly which words are underlined. This is therefore an unswept gap in a uniform convention, not an alternate convention. None of the reject criteria apply: the underline information is not present in reflowed or adjacent form anywhere, it is not page-break furniture or line wrapping, and it changes meaning - without it the transcription equally permits reading DELIMITED, POINTER or TALLYING as omissible and BY, WITH or IN as mandatory, which is the opposite of the standard's rule under 5.2.6.2.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is accurate as written; two additional defects in the SAME figure were found during verification and should be fixed in the same sweep. (1) LOST CHOICE INDICATORS. Looking at the printed glyphs of the ON OVERFLOW group: on each side there is an outer square bracket with visible top and bottom serif corners, and immediately inside it a plain FULL-HEIGHT VERTICAL BAR WITH NO CORNERS - the choice indicator. The markdown renders this as `⌐ ⌐ ... ¬ ¬` over `| | ... | |`, i.e. two corner glyphs per side, which draws a second NESTED BRACKET rather than a bracket plus a bar. Per 5.2.6.4 a bracket enclosing choice indicators means zero or more of the alternatives, each at most once, in ANY ORDER - so UNSTRING may carry neither phrase, ON OVERFLOW alone, NOT ON OVERFLOW alone, or BOTH IN EITHER ORDER. Rendered as a plain nested bracket that permission is lost. This is precisely the construct the START (line 31763) and STRING (line 31974) figure notes each flag with a ⚠, so UNSTRING needs the same ⚠ note. (2) FRAGMENTED FIGURE. In the PDF 14.9.48.2 is one continuous syntax diagram, but the markdown splits it across two code fences (lines 32377-32382 and 32388-32393) with `UNSTRING identifier-1` (32375), the `INTO …` line (32384), `[ WITH POINTER identifier-7 ]` (32385), `[ TALLYING IN identifier-8 ]` (32386) and `[ END-UNSTRING ]` (32395) left OUTSIDE any fence as ordinary Markdown prose, so the general format never renders as a single monospaced diagram and its alignment is not preserved. Minor cosmetic note: both fences close with `L ... ⌐`, using the top-left corner glyph ⌐ for the bottom-RIGHT corner. Also, the figure's true line span is 32372-32395 (the claim wrote 32372-32392, which stops before the `[ END-UNSTRING ]` line); this does not affect the finding.
